gloss: to implement; to carry out; to enforce

definitions.gloss: to implement, to carry out, to execute, to put into effect
definitions.explanation: To put a plan, policy, survey, or event into action. A formal word very commonly used in official, governmental, and business contexts.

examples.japanese: アンケートを{実施|じっし}する。
{避難|ひなん}{訓練|くんれん}が{実施|じっし}された。
examples.english: An evacuation drill was carried out.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{制度|せいど}は{来年度|らいねんど}から{実施|じっし}される{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: The new system is scheduled to be implemented starting next fiscal year.

notes:
One of the most common formal verbs in Japanese. Appears constantly in news, official announcements, and business documents. Often used in passive form {実施|じっし}される.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {調査|ちょうさ}を{実施|じっし}する: to conduct a survey/investigation
- {訓練|くんれん}を{実施|じっし}する: to carry out training
- {計画|けいかく}を{実施|じっし}する: to execute a plan
- {実施|じっし}{日|び}: implementation date
- {実施|じっし}{要項|ようこう}: implementation guidelines

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行|おこな}う: to carry out, to conduct — slightly less formal, also very common
- {施行|しこう}する: to enforce (a law) — specifically for putting laws into effect
- {実行|じっこう}する: to execute, to carry out — emphasizes actually doing it, can be used for personal actions too
